utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you are to continue with your examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Milosevic: [Continued]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, we went through documents from which one can see how many people were killed and abducted; citizens, soldiers, policemen, Albanians, Serbs, Montenegrins, and other ethnicities. Could you tell us briefly, as we reached tab 60, having finished with 59, what is under tabs 60, 61, very briefly, please.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In tab 60 we have the photo documentation of the criminal act of terrorism against a certain Dobrosav --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't hear the last name.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- who was found in June 1999 with his throat slit and decapitated. He was a shepherd, taking care of his herd, and the cattle were stolen by the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about 61?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is also a photographic documentation of the terrorist act committed in the area of Kacanik. Right outside Kacanik, if you go from Skopje, Georgi Stefanov and Stojmen Dimitrijevski were killed in the most monstrous way while travelling in a vehicle with Skopje licence plates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said Skopje.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right. It happened on the 10th of June, 1999.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I would like these two tabs exhibited as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, in tabs 52 and 53, to which we will not return, we could see how many attacks there were on the police and the army and how many people were killed in those attacks. I am now asking you, were any of these attacks provoked in any way by the army or the police?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No terrorist attack or provocation was ever provoked by the army or the police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me about this dispatch signed by you in tab 62.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's dated 14 March 1999. It contains information about a terrorist attack on an army vehicle on the road Suva Reka-Stimlje in the area of the Crnoljevo gorge. A soldier was injured in the attack and was transported by the traffic police to a hospital in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is just one example of such attacks. Similar attacks are to be found in tabs 20 to 26. We will not go back to them. This is an example of the documentation compiled in such attacks.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we have an armed provocation against members of the police or the army or the citizens, a dispatch was sent to all superior authorities, in this case, the Staff and the competent administrations of the ministry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, do any of these attacks relate to allegations in the indictment?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are attacks on the army and the police in that region that were reported by Colonel Janicevic to his superior authorities, and they pre-date the charges in the indictment, the events charged in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is their significance for your case?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The significance lies in the fact that in a couple of minutes we are going to come to Racak, which is one of the main points in what Mr. Nice calls the indictment, and these are the circumstances under which this terrorist organisation came into existence. All these circumstances point to an extremely intensive terrorist activity. You see the large number of soldiers, policemen, and civilians killed and the high degree of terror in this very small region. I don't know if you need to see the map again. We have seen it hundreds of times already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, well, we'll wait to see their significance in relation to Racak.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You were also able to see other types of activities when we were looking at events involving loss of life, what happened with terrorists and victims in various incidents. We took the example of Kacanik and other places that are also mentioned in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you tell me about these terrorist attacks. You said they were reported to all the competent authorities. Was the OSCE Verification Mission also notified?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every attack, every provocation, every incident was reported to the Verification Mission, both the people -- or, rather, both the incidents that happened while they were there and the incidents that happened a couple of months before they arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I must let you know that the Chamber is concerned about the use that you're making of the time allocated to you. Some of these matters we have been over. For example, Racak, which you say you are coming to, we have been over that. You have utilised most of the time allocated to you and you are still on Kosovo. You still have witnesses to call on Kosovo. We have Bosnia and Croatia to deal with. And please don't give me the standard answer that this merely illustrates the inadequacy of the time allocated to you by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will try to hurry up and use my time as rationally as possible, Mr. Robinson. And as for Racak, you say we have reviewed, Mr. Janicevic was in charge of precisely that area. That is, in the strictest sense of the word, his competency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked you whether OSCE Verification Mission members were also notified of all the incidents. I'm now asking you about the documents we have under tab 64 with all its subtabs from 1 to 28. I wanted us to go through them as efficiently as possible. Do we see reports, Official Notes, and notifications sent to the OSCE Verification Mission concerning terrorist attacks and anti-terrorist operations as well as other security related events?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We see reports of the Ministry of the Interior, notifications of the Ministry of the Interior to SC KVM, and all security related events of particular interest that happened in the area of our secretariat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Starting with 64.1 until 64.28, we have 28 reports drafted in the usual prescribed form. We see the first one. It says, "Contact with," and then members of the OSCE mission are indicated. The contact itself is described, and then --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The particular members of the mission, the topics of the exchange, and the answers they were given to their questions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In 64.2, .3, until .28, we see only that kind of reports concerning contacts with the OSCE-KVM. Is that the contents of tab 64 containing 28 such reports?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. Precisely.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, do you wish me to go through each one of these or can tab 64, from 1 to 28, be treated as one exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, perhaps it would be helpful if you just went through one, perhaps not in as summary a manner as you have done, so that we could then get a flavour of what these documents contain.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us look at 64.2. What does this Official Note dated December 1998 contain? Could you explain briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't want you to read it. Since you're familiar with it, then you can just give us the gist of it, Mr. Janicevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The gist of this document is that a team from the OSCE mission, including representatives from France, Germany, and some other country, I can't see which here, visited the police station in Nerodimlje, which is part of the Urosevac police station, to make inquiries, general inquiries about various incidents and events. They were given a report on what was going on in that area and what was going on that the Serbs were upset over the kidnapping, the recent kidnapping of two persons. There were no clues, but the Serbs knew that the kidnappings were done by terrorists based near Jezerce. That is the gist of it. They asked verifiers to extend their assistance in resolving this problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which the verifiers were unable to do, as far as I can see.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They came later, and they said they could not do anything. In fact, for the entire duration of the mission, they could not do anything about it in the whole area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tab 64.3 we see a report from the police station in Stimlje concerning their contact with the OSCE Verification Mission.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Commander of this police station, Branko Mladenovic, did have a meeting with OSCE verifiers who happened to visit just as a citizen was reporting his own kidnapping and the fact that he had been kept for ten days in some basement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: An Albanian or a Serb?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was an Albanian. He gave his account in the presence of OSCE verifiers. He described the whole event, for how many days he had been detained, what he had been given to eat, and how he had been treated.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the next page, because it has to do with Racak. It is on the fifth line, and he says, "I confirm the fact that in the same way a number of persons were kidnapped by Siptar terrorists who were located in the village of Petrovo, Racak, Malopoljce and Rance."

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that what it says there?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly what it says there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then a few lines further down, it says that there was a terrorist band in the village of Racak, Petrovo, Malopoljce and Rance. Can you tell us, Racak, Petrovo, Malopoljce and Rance, are they all neighbouring villages? And you've explained to us the actions of the 161st Brigade there; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Racak is about two and a half kilometres away from the centre of Stimlje but actually their suburbs follow on from one other and it looks like one settlement. Petrovo is about two kilometres away from Racak, and so is Malopoljce, two and a half kilometres. Rance is about three kilometres away. So all of the villages are in one area and follow on one from another. They're next door to each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This report on the talk with the Verification Mission -- or, rather, when was that meeting held? What does it say in the upper left-hand corner? What's the date there?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was conducted on the 4th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's January 1999, you say.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the police station of Stimlje; right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that police station covers the area of Racak, does it not?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does cover Racak and the other villages mentioned.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How far is Stimlje away from Racak? You said from the centre to Racak is two and a half kilometres.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right, two kilometres. But their suburbs are joined. They follow on from one another.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, why were these meetings with the OSCE mission held?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Pursuant to an agreement reached which provided for the fact that meetings be held at least once a week with the representatives of OSCE to exchange information which were of a security nature. However, although it was envisaged that those talks be held once a week, we were in contact with representatives of the Verification Mission on a daily basis. We informed them every day about the events that had taken place, security related, which were of interest and which took place on the area covered by the secretariat from the -- from day-to-day, on a 24-hour basis, and sometimes even more frequently. And those contacts were sometimes even held several times in a single day with the same group of verifiers. For example, if I can quote you one --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. Thank you. You have explained.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not to go through all of these documents, look at 64.5. It refers to the police station of Stimlje once again, and the date is the 9th. No it's not. The number is 9. I made a mistake. I read the wrong line. The date is the 11th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, the Chamber will allow you to tender these collectively.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just let us have the numbers. It's 64, tab 64.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, from 64.1 to 64.28 inclusive.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just to let you know, you skipped tab 63. I take it it's intentional.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I skipped 63, tab 63, inadvertently.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, just tell us what is in tab 63. It's a statement. Is it an official document of your secretariat of the interior?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is an official document of the SUP of Urosevac. The statement was taken by Sparavalo from this individual who indicated that certain persons were located in the leadership of the Staff of the 161st Brigade in Kacanik.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May this tab be exhibited, too, Mr. Robinson, please, tab 63, 64.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were saying that you informed the verifiers on a regular basis about all the events that took part. Now, what did the verifiers do? What steps did they take?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to what I know and to the best of my knowledge, as far as I was informed, they never -- we never had feedback. They never informed us what steps they had taken except in one case when they went to Gornje Nerodimlje police station and conveyed to the commander there that they were not able to find the person responsible for the area, the person in charge of the area, to discuss the question of the abducted Serbs from Nerodimlje. Otherwise, later on, they would only take note of the information conveyed to them from us and the security related incidents would be noted, but what they actually undertook I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell us just briefly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What were they supposed to do? According to the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they were supposed to -- according to the agreement, they were supposed to extend assistance to the police and to the army and members of terrorist organisations or, rather, Albanian citizens who were jeopardised, who were under jeopardy, who were considered to be under jeopardy by the police; and as far as I know, there were no such persons. 90 per cent of the verifiers asked to be involved in the problems themselves. They sought information about kidnapped persons, and they received those facts and figures, but we never received any feedback information from them except in that one case as to what they had actually undertaken.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the arrival of the Verification Mission, did the terrorist -- number of terrorist attacks decline? Were there fewer?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite the contrary. There was an increase of terrorist attacks after the arrival of the Verification Mission. Pursuant to the agreement, the army withdrew from all the positions which it had held up until the arrival of the verifiers, and of course the police did, too. They withdrew from the checkpoints that they had held. And in a gorge at Crnoljevska gorge, pursuant to the agreement, there was a post still held by the police and the army had stationed a combat group close by at Canovica Brdo. That was pursuant to the agreement, but there were provocations every day both in the presence of the verifiers and when they were not there. Every day, provocations and attacks and kidnappings, and this resulted very often in the death of innocent citizens. Probably the verifiers couldn't wield too much influence on the terrorists who engaged in actions like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about any attacks on members of the verifiers themselves by the terrorists? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one case which was not reported, but the police observation post, which was along the riverbanks towards Jezerce, some two and a half kilometres from Nerodimlje in the direction of Jezerce, they heard and saw a burst of gunfire on two -- two vehicles, and as far as I remember, there was one vehicle belonging to the OSCE and the other to KDOM. And the vehicles turned round and went back in the direction of Nerodimlje when this shooting took place. This incident was reported, and the policeman who was on duty in the station went out to ask the verifiers whether they needed any aid and assistance, but they didn't stop when the stop sign was shown them. They just carried on. And later on, when we tried to learn what had actually happened by talking to the verifiers, we didn't actually manage to get any information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was an Official Note written about the incident, and it was 64.10; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, are you saying that the attacks increased after the verifiers came because, pursuant to the agreement, the army and the police left the areas that they had secured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the agreement, the army and police left the territory or, rather, the positions that they had held previously in order to secure the settlements in the area and the population there. Once the army had withdrawn, the terrorists took over those positions. For example, Jezerce is a village which is in the area of the SUP Urosevac territory, towards Suva Reka and Budakovo, along that axis. In Jezerce, we would have patrols up until the 10th of October, 1999, patrolling the area. After that, the patrols were restrictive. Once the verifiers arrived -- however, once the verifiers arrived, we never were able to go there again. And the same thing happened with the village of Racak, Petrovo, and Malopoljce. After the second half of October, we were not able to enter those villages or areas. Whenever a police patrol would turn up at the access to the village, they would shoot at us. In the Crnoljevska gorge we had eight observer posts and they were reduced to six.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janicevic. Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, we're now going to move on to Racak. You explained the position of Racak to us, and you have a map in front of you, I believe.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: May the map be shown on the ELMO. Can you indicate the position of Racak on the map in relation to Stimlje and Urosevac, that is to say the area you were in charge of.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The scale is 1:50.000, and Stimlje is somewhere here. I don't know if you can see this. The scale is 1:50.000. That is Stimlje. Racak is two and a half kilometres away, right where I'm pointing now. That's Racak. Petrovo is to the south-east of Racak, here, a few kilometres away. And Malopoljce, about two and a half to three kilometres. A maximum of three kilometres away. Rance is situated in this sector here, at about four kilometres distance away from the Racak. Belince is to the north of Racak and is about one to one and a half kilometres away. This is the regional road running from Prizren to Suva Reka, Prizren -- and Prizren [as interpreted], and the regional road linking Stimlje to Urosevac. This is another road to Lipjan and Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, I assume that your excellent knowledge of geography on a microlevel is not only the result of your being able to map read but also through the fact that you were in the area. You knew the area. Is that right? Would that be the correct assumption?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is right. As an operative -- as a policeman and later on as an operative working on crime suspension and crime -- I worked in the Stimlje area and covered that sector, and I was always on the road to Racak, Petrovo, Malopoljce, and touring the other villages in the region, Topila, Canovica, and so on, along the mountain range here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Now, tell me, what knowledge did the SUP of Urosevac have, headed by you, about the presence and activity of KLA terrorists in Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The SUP of Urosevac, as can be seen from the Official Notes and reports and information received, knew that in the Racak area there were members of the 161st Terrorist Brigade, which had established a substaff in Racak, headed by Afet Bilalli, nicknamed Qopa, who was the commander of that so-called substaff, and the numerical strength of the group was about 80. There were about 80 members. Furthermore, our knowledge indicated that that terrorist group, on a daily basis, moved around the area, cruised the area and attacked. Police patrols, military patrols, civilians, regardless of their ethnicity, they stopped traffic along the road, kidnapping people on buses, for example. That happened several times, and also kidnapped people in passenger vehicles. People would disappear, no trace of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. You've just told us what the targets of the attack were, that is, the group working in Racak, what they did and whom they attacked. We now have, in tab 65 -- if you can turn to tab 65. From 65.1 to 65.28, and then in tab 66, from 66.1 to 66.44. So this is a large number of documents that we will have to go through selectively, I hope, if Mr. Robinson allows us to deal with it that way, as a set of documents. Now, in order for you to be able to follow --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It appears that the ones which are translated all have the name Jasovic and Sparavalo on them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm going to tell you which tabs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: No, is that correct? All the ones that are translated are documents compiled by Jasovic and Sparavalo?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's not the way I looked at them, who compiled them, because all of them are official documents of the Urosevac SUP. What I wish to say to you is that in tab 65, 65.2, that is Exhibit 295, tab 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I take it that all the ones with Jasovic and Sparavalo's names on them have already been exhibited?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure. I have the exact ones that were admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, how many of them were admitted already?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'll tell you. Out of these in tab 65, 17 was admitted. Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My machine doesn't work, so I can't --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nineteen. Nineteen were admitted, and I will give you the exact number of each and every one that was admitted, the number under which it had been admitted, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What's the point of going over documents we've been over already with the person who actually compiled them? Why do it again?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because this is a set of documents that Mr. Janicevic had at his disposal as chief of the Secretariat of the Interior of Urosevac. He is speaking about all this information that has to do with Racak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Higgins.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just attempt to clarify a certain matter? We have tried to undertake and have undertaken a review of the Jasovic files and the Stevanovic files to try and attempt to see which of the tabs have been previously admitted where they refer to Jasovic and Sparavalo. Those comments are listed on the index. And as far as our review is concerned, some of those documents which contain the name Jasovic have not been exhibited before. That is to the extent of the review that we've been able to undertake, and it appears that they are new documents. If I can just summarise what it appears to be. Tab 65, for example, relates to KLA activity in 1998, and more precisely, the presence and activity of Racak, the KLA in Racak, for example, tabs 65.9, 65.10, 65.12. Tab 64, again activities of the KLA in 1998 and, I think, some 1999. But to assist Your Honours, the review has been undertaken, and we've tried to locate as many of them as we can, and it seems that many of these have not been previously exhibited.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it appears that everybody is doing the work that ought to have been done by the accused. We certainly embarked upon an exercise that will be reduced to a schedule form for you that should identify in due course what material is new and potentially significant. It's not yet ready. It's quite labour intensive. It may be ready, I'm not sure, but it will be ready in due course; if not today, on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, you were the chief of the Urosevac SUP.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And were you -- where were you on the day of the Racak incident on the 15th of January?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the 15th of January, when the anti-terrorist action in Racak was carried out, I was at the police station in Stimlje from 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Did you hear that? The interpreters are asking you to speak up, speak more loudly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 15th of January, when the anti-terrorist action in Racak was carried out, from 7.00 a.m. I was at the police station in Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And when did you first learn of what happened?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What do you mean "what happened"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Of the Racak incident on the 15th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] An anti-terrorist action was carried out on the 15th of January and I was following via radio everything that was going on in Racak. I was following it through the radio communications that we had with the people who were directly engaged in this on the ground.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So you're another witness who wasn't actually involved in what took place, didn't actually kill anybody, but we're going to hear what you heard about the incident. Is that how you're going to present the evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't kill anyone, but I followed everything, and I worked out the plan for carrying out the anti-terrorist action in Racak.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, in respect of this evidence, you can, of course, lead the witness as to the information that he received by radio of what took place in Racak, and we'll hear that. As for the tabs, those that are new would obviously be very useful, but we are not able to identify with any certainty those that are new. Those that are old, if he has fresh information to give about them, anything new, then I mean to that extent we would hear it.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My microphone was off. Mr. Robinson, let us just deal with some confusion that's happened. Colonel Janicevic was not an observer of the action in Racak who just happened to be informed about what was going on there. He is the immediate superior of the policemen who were in action in the area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So Mr. Janicevic was in command position in Stimlje police station, commanding over the police force who is performing anti-terrorist act.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, I did not directly command anything. I mean, the anti-terrorist action was carried out by a group of policemen consisting of about 135 persons. One hundred policemen, members of the 64th Special Police Unit, and 30 members of the Operations Group. The action was directly commanded by Goran Radosavljevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But you told us earlier that you were receiving reports by radio.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, are we going to hear from Goran Radosavljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was not intending to call Goran Radosavljevic, but if Mr. Nice wants to hear him, he can. He can call him. He mentioned him in some interviews. But in relation to what happened in Racak, Mr. Janicevic knows everything.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because that police unit that carried out the anti-terrorist action was directly subordinated to him. It's his unit. He was not directly commanding in Racak itself, but he was in Stimlje on that day because this anti-terrorist action was taking place in Racak. That is the normal way things work in the ground. He is chief of the secretariat. He's a colonel. He's two and a half kilometres away from where the action is taking place. He is not directly commanding the company that is carrying out that anti-terrorist action. That is what is done by a commanding officer of a company.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Janicevic, you would not challenge that you were the first person for Mr. Radosavljevic to report?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. I was not someone who Mr. Radosavljevic reported to, but I was the superior of part of the group of policemen who were taking part in it. 105 policemen belonged to the SUP of Urosevac. Goran Radosavljevic was a member of the MUP staff, and on behalf of the staff he was appointed leader of that action, and that company that I was in charge of was attached to that group, in addition to the Operative Pursuit Group that was always under his command while we were in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The reports that you heard on the radio came from whom; Mr. Radosavljevic or from someone else?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From the commander of the company. I followed all the communications because there was a single communications line. Everybody listened to those communications that I was listening to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Who was the commander of the company providing the reports? Radosavljevic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. Radosavljevic was in charge of the entire action, whereas the commander of the company was --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not understand the name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please give the name of the person, the commander of the company who sent the reports by radio.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Major Milan Lecic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let me be clear about this again, Mr. Janicevic. Where was Mr. Radosavljevic located at the time of the operation? Was he with you in Stimlje?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. He was in the field. He was supposed to be in the field, actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. And if you could describe your role in relation to anti-terrorist act operation in Racak. What were you supposed to do? Why did you go to Stimlje, and what did you do there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The anti-terrorist action in Racak was carried out in the territory of the Urosevac SUP, and I was the chief of the SUP Urosevac. So Racak is within the territory where I was chief of secretariat. A company of mine took part in the action, and I was personally interested in lawfully completing this action without any omissions and doing it properly. That is number one. Number two, according to the task given to me by the Staff, I was in charge of following the action from Stimlje and informing the Staff every now and then about the course the action was taking and the results that were being achieved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, Mr. Milosevic, the Chamber wants to hear from the witness what he can tell from his experience without uselessly going over the documents which we have seen already.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, we have a set of documents here that I've been quoting from, tabs 65 and 66. You have seen some of them and you have not seen others, but the entire set of documents speaks of the situation in Racak and the terrorist activities and everything that the police had by way of information, everything that we could collect. And I can tell you straight away, since Mr. Nice said that this was an enormous job, it's a very simple job. Tab 65.2 was admitted into evidence as 295, tab 2.1. Tab 65.5 was admitted likewise. Tab 65.5 is tab 65.1 of Exhibit 295. Tab 65 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice -- I beg your pardon. Mr. Milosevic, tab 65.5 is an identical one with 65.1, which is -- which you presented. So this is an example how you are presenting your exhibits in an orderly manner. It is your responsibility. Can we not hear from the witness what he can tell from his experience and then coming back to these exhibits if necessary?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. That's what we'll do, Mr. Milosevic. Let the witness tell what he learned -- Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: -- about the incident. And I would encourage you to call Major Milan Lecic, who actually sent the reports. He was there on the day in the field, and he would probably be the best person to testify from the point of view of someone with firsthand knowledge of this very controversial incident.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I will move on through questions that have to do with his direct experience.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But before that, let us clear up one thing, Mr. Janicevic. Are all these documents under tab 65 and 66, 28 documents in tab 65 and some 44 in tab 66, are they all your documents of the Urosevac SUP, and did you have them all in your hands at the relevant time when they were drafted?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are all authentic, and they originate from the Urosevac SUP. I held each and every one of them in my hands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you hold each document in your hands at the time when it was drafted?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. And it was based on these documents that the plan was drafted for that anti-terrorist operation. We drew on these reports and other operative information we gathered in the field.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So they pre-date the anti-terrorist operation.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was based on the intelligence contained in these reports that we drew up our plan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. To the best of your knowledge, there were terrorist forces there. Based on what did you know that? You say the information is contained in these documents.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How about the sources of your intelligence? Were they exclusively from the area, gathered in the usual way in which the police gathers information?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are they contained in the reports and Official Notes, and are they indisputable facts that you established in the process of gathering information about terrorist activities?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In addition to these reports, there are also criminal reports against unidentified perpetrators guilty of very serious crimes. In that area, just before the anti-terrorist operation, there were 11 attacks involving loss of life against policemen and civilians. Before the 31st of December, 13 soldiers and officers got killed in that area, 25 officers and soldiers were seriously wounded, including two policemen. All this information was submitted to the Staff, together with a draft plan for this anti-terrorist operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Who submitted that plan?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Urosevac SUP, and I signed it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was you, your Secretariat of the Interior that, based on all these events and incidents reflected in these reports and information that you -- it was your secretariat that made the plan.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct. We made this plan to conduct an operation against the terrorists that were --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That were terrorising the whole population on a daily basis. So you had a group involved to deal with this terrorist group that had 80 members, as you said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could I ask you, do you have the plan with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Where is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know whether you know, but we had it in the building that housed our staff. It was made in one single copy. That kind of plan is signed by the superior commanding officer that was in charge of the operation. The whole building burnt down. 90 per cent of the documentation that would have been very useful for this trial burnt down, but it's not my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And the other documents that we're looking at, were they in the same building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. These are copies of the documents that were kept by the people, the actual officers and workers who were in charge of different cases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's Jasovic and Sparavalo in the case of the ones that they prepared.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not only Jasovic and Sparavalo. There is also Krstic and others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So these have come from the individuals who compiled them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Some of them kept copies for themselves. A policeman and an inspector had the right to keep a copy for his own personal file after sending a copy to his superior officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you bring these documents to The Hague or did they come some other way?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Part of the documents were brought by me. Another part was obtained by the associates of Mr. Milosevic in Belgrade from the Ministry of the Interior, and I brought some copies of the reports that I had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And did you actually get any copy documents from people who had compiled the reports and then kept copies for themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, some.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Going back to the plan, when the Staff approved the plan and it was sent back to you, did they not keep a copy?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Such plans are made in one single copy. After the implementation of the operation, the plan is returned to the Staff. After this operation, the Ministry of the Interior established a working group that analysed all the events before and after the implementation of this operation. That plan had to be returned to the Staff to serve as a basis for drafting a plan to clarify the circumstances that required this anti-terrorist operation to take place. That was the responsibility of the policemen who worked there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've lost me now. The plan was sent back from your office to Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, in Pristina. The MUP staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And this was to later -- at a later stage, to analyse these events. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After this anti-terrorist operation was over, the public prosecutor sent an application to the Staff to give him information that would serve as a basis for analysing the circumstances in which this operation took place. The MUP set up a working group to analyse all the facts and all the circumstances that had an influence on the course of the operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But my question was: Was the plan sent back to Pristina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is it still there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it was there until the bombing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There. I have before me index of exhibits with updated cross-references. That means everything is specified in great detail and precision. I hope we will be thus able to identify exactly what has been admitted and what hasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What matters to me, Mr. Janicevic, is this: These documents under tab 65 and 66, have you read reach one of them carefully, and did you read each one of them carefully at the time when they were written, for the purpose for which they were written?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Each document had to come to my desk. In addition to other officers, they had to be submitted to me. I read each one of them carefully, I saw what they were about, I saw what operative intelligence they contained, and with my subordinates at our regular briefings, we agreed what specific measures to take on the basis of this information.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In tab 66, we also have a great number of statements taken from a certain number of persons who are indubitably Albanian, judging by their names.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are persons who, under various circumstances, came to contact with the police or who came to the police of their own accord. Interviews were conducted with them to discuss the presence, the activities, and crimes committed by the KLA in that area.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me draw your attention, gentlemen, for instance, in tab 66, out of 44, only about 20 have been admitted already.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you know which ones?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know exactly, exactly. So in tab 66, previously admitted were 66.4, .7, 9, 10, 11 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic is kindly asked to read more slowly, especially numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 19, 20, 22, 23, 27, 29.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter has missed some.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 32, 33, 34, 35, 36, 41, and that's it. These have been admitted already.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Several of the others aren't translated, of course. And it's not just a question of knowing which documents have been produced before. That's not the exercise on which I am engaged. The exercise on which I'm engaged is to see what if any relevance there is in any of these documents on the matters before us. That's, of course, additionally difficult to do if they're not translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As we indicated, Mr. Milosevic, given that this witness is the most immediate person to the operation that took place in Racak, can we not hear from him what he learned from his experience, and then we can come back to these exhibits later.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have just explained what kind of information you had about terrorist activities. What kind of knowledge did you have about the fortifications and all the other installations that existed in Racak before you ordered this operation to be carried out?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, let us move directly to the information that he received on the day of the incident. We have had enough information now about the background and the incidents that led to the January 15th attacks. He told us that he received information by radio. We want to find out what he heard.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you are not interested in anything that preceded and that motivated this operation planned by the Secretariat of the Interior in Urosevac, as signed and prepared by Mr. Janicevic, Colonel Janicevic, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are you referring to evidence which we have already have in relation to the killing of two Serb policemen?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you have heard Colonel Janicevic explain that it was not only two policemen who were killed. It was a whole series of terrorist activities involving the killing of 12 persons that preceded this anti-terrorist action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have the context.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have had enough, so why don't you go straight to the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's clear up this. You just mentioned this plan. That plan was approved. Who approved it?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chief of Sector, Vlastimir Djordjevic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many policemen were engaged in the implementation of the operation, from your secretariat and from the Staff?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One hundred five members of the Special Police Unit and 30 members of the Operations Pursuit Group.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These 105 members were from your secretariat and you are their immediate superior?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've had all this information. You've been instructed what to do. We ought to terminate this if you're not going to do as instructed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I have to lay the foundation for my following question, which is: What was the mission? What was the task of that -- of those members of the Special Police Unit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: We've had all the details of the numbers who were there and who was responsible for what. So let's get to the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who could you have heard the details from, please? If the superior officer of that Special Police Unit was here, I assume it was up to him to say what kind of task the unit had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That's your next question, but you've just gone over yet again the numbers of officers who were there which he's already told us in great detail. If you were listening to the answers to the questions, you would know that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not asking about the numbers. I've heard the numbers. I asked what task that Special Police Unit had.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I answer?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, answer that question and let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to the plan, the assignment of the Special Police Unit company was to block the village of Racak from the Stimlje axis and Beric [phoen] and Petrovo. The task of the Operational Pursuit Group which was trained and underwent a number of training sessions in anti-terrorist combat was to enter into the rear in-depth of the village where the terrorists were located during the night; in the early hours of the morning, in fact. According to the plan, the pursuit group set out at 3.00 and fully took control of the trenches and positions held by the terrorists sometime until 6.30. The special police company started to effect the blockade of the village at about 6.30 a.m., and the operation went on until about 7.00 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you reached Stimlje; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I reached Stimlje then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you were able to follow the operation yourself?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And at that same time, approximately at that time, two vehicles turned up with the verifiers, who had been informed about the anti-terrorist operation that was under way.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please, before I ask my next question, who informed the verifiers? Who was it who did that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The verifiers were informed by Colonel Mijatovic, the deputy head of the Staff in Pristina, at the headquarters in Pristina, and the police station commander Branko Mladenovic on their outstation in Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So you were in Stimlje --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move on, when you say the verifiers showed up, where were they?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were stationed at two positions which was the -- were the best vantage points from which they were able to observe the operation. They had -- they saw the whole of Racak as if it were in the palm of their hands, and if they observed properly, then they were able to see every single thing that went on, and I'm sure they did do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I saw their vehicles and people around the vehicles, but I didn't approach them because I watched them from a distance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: At what time did you see them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it was around 7.00 in the morning, when I myself arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that the only time that you saw them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw them later on when I left the police station, in the yard. Because from the yard of the police station in Stimlje, you can see the points and positions at which the verifiers were. Stimlje is not a large town. It's a -- it's a village, slightly larger village, but could you see the position of one group and the other group. And around 10.00 on that same day, the group that was at the entrance to Racak itself, coming in from the direction of Stimlje and the old people's home there, another vehicle joined them. So that would make a total of three groups of verifiers observing the operation throughout the day, practically the whole time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we have been through this before.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's your responsibility to identify --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And no doubt this is part of the Racak binder, I assume. Let's go on in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, please. Take a look at just a few of these photographs and tell us whether you can state -- whether you can see the positions of the verifiers on any of those photographs.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course you can see their positions. You can see them on both these photographs, on both places. One group of verifiers was in this part here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mean on the hill?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the hill. On the opposite side from which this photograph was taken.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this photograph, the photograph of this area, you could see from the position where the verifiers were?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The group of verifiers was at that point here, and there was another group of verifiers -- this is the school building here, the primary school in Stimlje, and some 250 to 300 metres above the school was another group of verifiers. They could see -- the first group could see both this hamlet here and this part of the village there, in addition to the hill up here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So everything that was marked by Mr. Nice here, they could see all that?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, everything.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Any other photographs that you consider useful?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ah, here's another one. Here you can see it more clearly. The verifiers were here. They were here, and they were in this area here, above the school building, between the Kostanje feature and the school itself, and both groups could see this area here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, tell us, what is the distance, roughly, between the place the verifiers were standing at and this area here?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the first group standing here by the old people's home is not further than 5 to 600 metres away. This other group might have been at a distance of one kilometre, perhaps. Probably a kilometre, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We see the references here on the map, so I think it is easy to identify what the points are. I took the maps later on, not while preparing and proofing the witness. I found these maps later on, after I had talked to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Anyway, thank you, Mr. Janicevic. Now -- yes, what did you want to say?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's another photograph here where we can see the fortifications in that part of the village. Here you can see the trenches which come out to the bunkers, and a second line of trenches behind them, behind the village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, could the verifiers see that as well?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The verifiers knew that the trenches existed. They knew that bunkers existed. They knew that there was shooting, and there was shooting done in their presence, both at the police station and, on one occasion, as far as I was informed, from a 12.7 millimetre weapon. From the Kostanje feature they shot at the police station when the verifiers were inside. So there is no logic that they could not have noticed any of that. That doesn't hold water.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This should be Exhibit 156.4, Mr. Nice's set of documents, these photographs. I think it should be 156.4, but I'll check again.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I found something else on this photograph. May I tell you? This second group that was by the school building --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about the second group of verifiers?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the second group of verifiers, by the primary school building. They were a little further off from where the events took place, but they might have had an even better view because they had --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness repeat what they had? Could the witness repeat what they had, the verifiers, in order to see better.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please repeat what you just said, Mr. Janicevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The second group of verifiers, which was located at the Kostanje position and feature by the primary school in Stimlje, there is this hill here, you can see that on the monitor, on the screen, and they could see, that group could see everything happening on the neighbouring hill above the village of Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In the area that you're indicating to?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the area I'm indicating now. The distance is about one kilometre. And they had very good optic sites, all of them, they were equipped with good optic sites and were able to take photographs. And I think that some did film it using a video camera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janicevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to remind you, gentlemen, that yesterday we talked about distances, referring to another matter, what could be seen at 10, 11, 12, 13 kilometres, and here we're talking about a distance of just one kilometre, which even with the naked eye can be seen. It was one kilometre at the most, and Mr. Janicevic said perhaps 500 or 600 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you saw the verifiers at 7.00 in the morning. When you arrived, they were already there.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I reached this area, I saw a group of verifiers next to the police and military point at Kostanje, their yellow vehicle and another vehicle government above the special institute, at the institute at the entrance to Racak, the houses, because the police station is not more than 200 metres away from the institution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, can we see the place where you were located at the time from this picture?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not on this photograph because it's behind this hill here. So behind the hill where the first group of verifiers was standing. Perhaps 20 metres. The altitude was 20 metres lower than them, than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We've often enough proceeded on the basis of people pointing at maps and not getting them to mark them, but on this occasion it may be the Chamber would conclude that this map ought to be marked by the witness with where he says people were placed -- this photograph ought to be marked by the witness with places where he says people were placed, not least so that if other witnesses come, whereas, for example, the verifiers are identified, they can note precisely what's being said about -- it's also quite difficult to recall sufficiently accurately what the witness may have been intending to identify as the position of a verifier if it's not recorded in writing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I agree with you, Mr. Nice, that that would be helpful. We're going to take the break, and when we return we'll have those points marked on the maps. We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.text: Thank you, and on behalf of Mr. Milosevic, I express my gratitude to you. Mr. Janicevic, I'm going to ask you to mark on the maps the -- the photographs, rather, on the photographs, the areas where the verifiers were and where you were. Do we have the photographs there?

utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.text: That will be D313.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, the registrar will see to that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I would like to remind you and Mr. Kwon that a while ago when I played a videotape for you that was recorded at the time of the event in Racak, I showed on it the orange vehicles belonging to the verifiers, and they were on that videotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You've certainly played a videotape while I've been here and claimed that there were orange vehicles on it, but I couldn't at the time see them. So if you have an opportunity of playing that tape again, I would welcome it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Indeed, that's a position I endorse and I would be assisted myself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll try to find that tape over the weekend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As a matter of fact, I believe it can be found in the video material from the hearings, just like Mr. Kay found Paddy Ashdown's testimony and when that was shown. May I proceed now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, you explained what the task of the members of the Special Police Unit was. So what was the exact time when this unit carried out a blockade from the Stimlje-Petrovo-Belince direction?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The blockade was introduced exactly around 7.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the time when you arrived at the spot?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After that, this blockade that was placed from Stimlje, Belince and Petrovo Selo, did it start narrowing down?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the blockade was placed and after information was received that the trenches of the terrorists were taken by the members of the Operative Pursuit Group in the background of the village, the area was narrowed down. At the same time, the commander of the company used a megaphone, a loudspeaker, asking the terrorists to surrender, telling them that they were under a blockade and that they would be arrested. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, tell us how you're learning this. Is this something you saw or is this a report that you received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the report of the company commander.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And that is Mr. Milan Lecic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. I'm sorry, let me just add something to what I've said. The police station of Stimlje is 100 to 150 metres away from the place where the blockade starts, or basically where the village of Racak starts. It's in the depression and Racak starts on the hill. Cesta, as they call it. So when the blockade moved further on, at the same moment the company commander used a loudspeaker to ask them to surrender, and he repeated that for about 15 times until gunfire was opened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This information you received by radio? This information you received by radio?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The first call I heard myself, when he first called upon them to surrender, and after that, over the radio.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What time was it? What time was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Around 7.00 in the morning. I cannot tell you the exact time, but it was, say, 7.00 or five past seven.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did the operation not start at 3.00, earlier than 7.00?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Part of the operation started at 3.00 in the morning. Part of the operation involving the Operative Pursuit Group that had the task of taking the trenches or, rather, getting to the terrorists from the back and making it impossible for them to escape towards the hamlet of Luzak and Petrovo Selo and the other villages where they were behind. This Operative Pursuit Group of the police did not have the task to narrow down the terrain. Their task was to wait for the terrorists and also to call upon them to surrender if they come across them. The task of the company was to narrow down the blockade and to possibly arrest the terrorists, if they would agree to be arrested; if they didn't open fire, that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you're saying that the combat did not take place Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. until 7.00, did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Open combat did not take place before 7.00, except for the combat during the night from 3.00 until 5.30 when three or four terrorists were killed who were at the positions that they had taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What were you doing while that combat was taking place overnight?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The morning? I was not there. But I was informed at 7.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Where were you and what was -- what were you doing at 3.00, from 3.00?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was in Urosevac. When I arrived in Stimlje, they told me that the Operative Pursuit Group had taken up positions where the terrorists had been until then and that they were waiting for the narrowing down of the blockade by the PJP company from the direction of Belince.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you explained just now that the Operative Pursuit Group, before the blockade got narrowed down, took those trenches.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was not much fighting there because there were only a few members of the KLA there who were guarding the trenches?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Only two?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then when they took the trenches, they were waiting for a Special Police Unit to start narrowing down the blockade from the area of Stimlje?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To introduce a total blockade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I just wanted to see whether I understood you correctly, what you were saying. So you heard the first call over the loudspeaker to surrender. You heard that yourself. And then you heard them over the radio.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the terrorists respond to this call to surrender?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single one. As for the first call, the --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I wonder if I could interrupt.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: The leading question, which was clearly intentional, is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is a summary of what is the evidence so far, I take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's the evidence already.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well, but it's a -- it's the bit about taking the trenches, waiting for the special --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: That wasn't the previous --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No. Now, that is a critical part of this narrative, as the accused well knows from the documents I've explored, and it may be that the Chamber would think it prudent to take the questioning away from the accused and to find out exactly what and with what sources this witness is able to give this part of the narrative. It is a critical part of the narrative. I'll do it, of course, in cross-examination otherwise, but that question seemed to me to be pretty monstrous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You can do it in cross-examination, as you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So be it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Janicevic, you've just described now what was going on. Could you please put on the overhead projector a map of Racak, and could you explain to us on that map the beginning of the operation, how it evolved, the positions of the members of the MUP, of the terrorists, and how the operation developed. I would like to draw your attention to 70.1, the development of the situation from 3.00 until 8.30 a.m. In tab 70.2, a map including the development of the situation from 8.30 until 10.00, and in the following tab from 10.00 until 1530 hours. Could you please explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Before we race ahead, if we're going to be looking at these maps, it may be that the Court would be assisted by knowing something about by whom and when the maps were drawn and for what purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I was about to ask. If you could answer the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The maps were prepared in preparation of this trial, in Belgrade, in cooperation with Milan Lecic, commander of the PJP company, before I came here.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There's a problem for Chamber, in my respectful submission. We are now, it would appear, being offered hearsay material, prepared for the purposes of the litigation, by someone who it appears is not coming. Because when the Chamber invited the accused to call him, or suggested how wise it would be to call him, the accused characteristically didn't answer the question and gave an answer to a different question, the preceding procedural issue that the Chamber had raised with him, in much the same way as he's declined, despite Radosavljevic being on his witness list, ever to come clean about whether he's going to call him. Now apparently not. Now, these documents, it would seem to me, may offend the Chamber's approach to hearsay material.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, let me clarify this: Were you involved in the preparation of this map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic, proceed.
