utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please explain, using this map, how the operation started and how it developed; the position of MUP members, the position of KLA members, and how the situation developed.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me explain the legend first, if you allow me. Blue designates the Siptar terrorist forces in the field and the positions they were occupying. Red is for VJ forces. The circle with an arrow is the direction of movement of MUP members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. I understand the colour version is not offered to the Prosecution. No?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And how, if I may ask --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: -- through the Court, how am I supposed to be able to deal with colour-coded maps in preparation for cross-examination if I'm only provided with black and white? It simply won't do.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will provide the Prosecution with my own copies of these maps in colour. And I will ask the AV booth -- these are three different maps for three different times. I will ask the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is it tab 70.1 which is now on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I can note it by the time. It starts from 3.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Is the witness able to say or --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson -- excuse me, Mr. Janicevic, just a minute. I would like to ask the video engineers to sharpen the colours, because we cannot see them very well on the projector, the red, blue, and green.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, they would have heard that. Let's see whether that can be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While it is being prepared, Mr. Janicevic, bear in mind when you answer the question put by the accused, please indicate as how you did come to know those facts; whether you heard that in person or whether you heard that in recent preparation for your testimony. Do you follow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand. Can I start?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you first answer Mr. Kwon's question. Mr. Kwon asked you a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. You bear in mind in answering each question to indicate as how you come to know each fact. Can you go back to the VJ position? You said VJ position.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Red designates VJ forces.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see anything on the screen here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 243 Motor Brigade.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 243 Motorised Brigade, correct. They were located on Canovica Brdo, below elevation 671.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let us clarify one thing: There was one unit of the 243rd Brigade there. Why was it there?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That unit of the 243rd Brigade was there to protect communications, pursuant to the agreement with the OSCE.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Pursuant to the agreement with the OSCE?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remind you, gentlemen, that in every area of Kosovo there was one unit, one company strong, to secure roads, and that is the location marked here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell us, Mr. Janicevic, that unit of the VJ, did it participate in any way in the anti-terrorist operation in Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Not a single soldier, not a single combat vehicle of this group or any other VJ group was involved in the anti-terrorist operation. I can say that with full responsibility.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You marked it exactly where it was positioned pursuant to the agreement, and that was the location where they were standing. There was no coordinated action or anything of the sort?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you cannot lead in these matters. You know that this is a controversial issue in the trial. You cannot lead. You cannot lead --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He answered. Mr. Robinson, prior to this, the witness replied. He said, and I'm summarising, not a single soldier of this group or any group was involved in Racak. Not a single unit of the army was involved in Racak. That's what he said before. He said, "I say with full responsibility that not a single soldier or vehicle were participating in the anti-terrorist operation in Racak." It's all on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Involvement in the operation could be one thing and coordination could be another. Please bear in mind the leading question is not helpful to the Chamber. Please proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Bearing in mind what Mr. Kwon said, was there any coordination with this army unit that you marked here?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the 14th of January, in the evening, before the operation began, there was a meeting and Krsman Jelic, commander of this unit of the 243rd Brigade, was invited to be acquainted with the plan of action. The person in charge of the operation, the company commander and platoon commanders were also attending the meeting. Krsman Jelic, commander of this army unit, was invited so as to know that if any combat occurs between terrorists and policemen, he shouldn't open fire on the policemen who were going to be in front of him. They had, in addition to this, two forward posts, one on the road with a combat vehicle Praga positioned there, manned by five or six soldiers, and another standing post on Kostanje hill, which you cannot see on this map, but it's approximately in the same area where the verifiers were. That's east of Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the basis for this information which you are providing? What's the source?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I saw it with my own eyes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Were you at the meeting on the 14th of January?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, who chaired that meeting of the 14th?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I chaired it, as chief of the secretariat and as somebody who was personally interested in having this operation carried out in that area to put a stop to terrorist activities and to put a stop to killings.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just received information that one of my associates found and prepared the videotape showing verifiers in Racak. If I may address the video engineers, this is a good time, a convenient time to play it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Let it be played.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] These are the vehicles of the verifiers that you see now. The police is coming in. Up on the hill are verifiers. It's enough. Thank you, video engineers. We can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: First of all, it would be helpful to be just reminded of the exhibit number for this exhibit, and it would also be helpful, if it hasn't been provided in the evidence so far, to know the provenance of the tape and also whether what we've seen is said to be a continuous passage of the tape. It's among a number of issues that arise from the tapes of that have been produced by the accused and in the course of the Racak material, and I'd certainly be grateful now to know a little bit more, if we can, about that tape as it's been shown. Or later, but preferably now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, can you say whether this is in evidence already; and, if so, what is the number?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This has been shown here, I'm certain of that. It was shown by me. I cannot tell you off-the-cuff which exhibit number it was or whether it has been admitted at all. At that time, I remember I thought everything played here was automatically admitted, and it was only later that you explained to me that I had to tender it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Ms. Dicklich I think has identified all the material, and it's 45. -- 290 tab 45.2, and it's said that the source -- 45.1, and it's said that the source is Reuters but we know no more than that. And I don't know whether this is an unbroken, I mean an uninterrupted passage of Reuters tape, and it was introduced through the witness Marinkovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. It was admitted on the 23rd -- 24th of March this year. And the source is Reuters. A Reuters team filmed this. They were accompanying the police and they filmed everything they could see in Racak. It's tab 290. It was played during the testimony of Investigating Judge Danica Marinkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you know when this was filmed, Mr. Milosevic, or the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was filmed on the 15th of January, in Racak, as the police entered. It is a longer video. You could see a much longer video. The police was just going into Racak. Fire hadn't been opened yet. You can see verifiers on the hill. And fire was opened on the police a bit later. What we just saw was the beginning of the blockade. That's D290, tab 45.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you said there was more to this tape.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, and you saw that material when I played it first. I believe I even played part of it during my opening statement or, rather, one of my opening statements, but I will try to play it again for you, if you wish, in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: My record says it lasts 6 minutes and 23 seconds, so it will not last that long. Ten, ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain, Mr. Janicevic, this first map that is on the overhead projector that explains how things developed from 3.00 a.m. to 8.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I left off when I was explaining the legend. This circle with the horizontal arrow is the direction of movement of the MUP. The curved line, the curved green line, are MUP forces. The blue circle, half coloured, is a bunker of the Siptar terrorist forces. The crossed circle are fallen terrorists. A circle with another horizontal arrow in blue is the direction of pull-out of the terrorists. The green square with the flag is the police station. Green rectangular, filled up to a diagonal line, is a police checkpoint; and a blue triangle is the observation post of the Siptar terrorist forces. The police station Stimlje marked, and the green circle with the arrow is the place from which the 6th Company of the PJP moved out at that time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you there in Stimlje in the police station beginning with Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 7.00 a.m.?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I was there all the time after that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the scale of this map?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I just gave my map to Mr. Nice, but I believe it's 1 -- I'm sorry, it's actually 1:12.500.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the scale is even larger. One square is 500 square metres, in reality. This is the position of the army. At this police checkpoint the Operative Pursuit Group moved out at 3.00 a.m. The Operative Pursuit Group moves through the woods until they reach the trenches occupied by the terrorists. At 5.00 a.m., they enter the trenches and take full control of them before 6.30, with the exception of one thing, and that is the observation post at Krcine. That was taken a bit later. From 5.00 a.m. to 6.30 a.m., in this time line, at 6.51 terrorist was killed in a bunker. At 6.45 two were killed who manned the observation post and a machine-gun nest below Krcine elevation. At 6.45, four terrorists were killed who had been moving to replace the group that had manned the trenches until then. They were to take over their shift. There were 3 terrorists plus one leader. At 7.15 the terrorists were already seized by panic. They had heard over the loudspeaker that they were surrounded. They heard --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute. It says in the transcript three terrorists plus one leader. That is the shift leader, shift leader, in fact. It is something like a sergeant. Shift leader. He is no leader, at least not in the political sense. It should be "shift leader."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask, what is the source of your knowledge of these events so far?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The company commander, Milan Lecic, was my subordinate. One of the leaders of this Operative Pursuit Group, late Miro Mekic, who was killed on the 19th of November, fighting terrorists who were trying to protect their positions, wrote a report after the operation was finished on the 18th of January, and based on that report, based on my own memory and the memory of the company commander, this account of the advance of the police in Racak and the whole time line of events from 3.00 to 8.30 was written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Do you have that report with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately not, and I explained why I didn't have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What happened to it, sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The report and almost all the documents relevant to this -- these proceedings were burnt when the building of the MUP in Pristina was bombed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the various people who were killed so far, how were they killed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, but how?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the armed settling of accounts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What weapons were used to kill them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May the witness continuing answering?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Go ahead, Mr. Janicevic.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the entrance to Racak, at the terrorist checkpoint next to the road from the Stimlje axis, at 0715 hours a terrorist was killed, and the police forces, to all intents and purposes, set up a siege or semi-siege around Racak until 8.30 a.m., by 8.30 a.m. There were no losses on the side of the police. The terrorists at the time, at about 7.15 a.m. tried to pull out towards the Hadzovici hamlet and the Luzak hamlet, which is part of Petrovo village.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that all?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that was the dynamics that went on there. Now let's see the events after 8.30 I think until 10.00 a.m. it was. I can't find the exact time. I have it here somewhere. Let me just take a moment to find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While it is being prepared, I should note that legend and chronology should be translated in due course.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do we see on the screen now?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the screen now we have the activities of MUP units from 8.30 a.m. until 10.00 of the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before you begin explaining what happened and the sequence of events and time line, does this legend on the map completely match the legend you've just explained to us?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. It fully matches it. Here we have the situation that occurred from 8.30 to 10.00 a.m. From 8.30 onwards, there was active fighting and armed resistance towards the police that were moving forward from the direction of Belinac, Stimlje, and part of the Petrovo-Racak road. At -- or, rather, between 9.00 and 10.00, another bunker was taken control of where there were two members of the terrorist group, and that is somewhere in the middle of the village. The village of Racak, of course. At that same time, another bunker was taken control of held by another group of policemen, and two more terrorists were killed in that operation. And in a third bunker, three terrorists were killed by 10.00 a.m. The terrorists, who were in the headquarters and the houses in which they had been accommodated, were armed and started in combat formation towards the trenches where members of the pursuit group, police group, were located. And as I said a moment ago, these were taken control of by 6.30 a.m. Without knowing that in the trenches there were members of the police, these same persons reached the trench -- almost reached the trenches. The policemen who were in the trenches themselves called to them to surrender. The terrorists were taken by surprise because they thought they had their own men in the trenches, and they opened heavy fire, targeting the police members of the pursuit group in the trench, and most of the terrorists were killed in that operation. So between 7.00 and 7.30, eight terrorists were killed in the northern side of the trenches behind the village of Racak. From 7.00 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Why does this now deal with from 7.00 to 7.30 when it bears to be from 8.30 until 10.00?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This map shows the time line and how the blockade was narrowed down by the PJP. The positions that were taken were taken from 3.00 a.m., and the position of the pursuit group did not change to the end of the operation. The people who were --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These deaths don't appear on the previous one you've just gone through.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They don't appear, but they're here on this map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what's your source of knowledge of these events that you're now describing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A report by the late Miro Mekic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So these aren't things that you were hearing going on. These are the result of a written report by your inferior officer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: From whom we're not going what hear; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You just described him as late.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, yes. He was killed in an operation on the 19th of January. Warrant officer. Here we don't have the time intentionally or the movement of the unit because this was a stationary unit, which from 6.30 a.m. took up their positions and remained there until the end of the operation. It was just the group of policemen that moved around under the command of Lecic. The 6th Police Company which narrowed down and tightened the blockade. So that's why it's not clear, these deaths and casualties are not quite clear here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Is that all in relation to that map?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me just explain how many people were killed there. From 7.30, on the northern side, eight persons were killed. On the southern -- or, rather, northern side of the trench. Six were killed at the bunker between 7.00 and 7.30, and seven were killed in the central part of the trenches. And from 7.00 to 7.30 or 7.35, other -- the others were killed in the bunker above the village, five others. PJP units until 10.00, the green lines there, from the western side. The west is here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: West of Stimlje, you mean?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, west of Stimlje from Racak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't understand that. Could you give me an explanation. Explain it to me. To the right we should have east. We should be looking east on the right.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you're quite right. At the same time, around 10.00, the terrorists were regrouping and re-organising from Petrovo. They sent reinforcements towards Hadzovici and the Red Road, as it was called, or the wall. And a group from the village of Luzak were moving towards the Krcine feature and above. On the left-hand side -- it reached the left-hand side at about 10.00 a.m. Then there was a clash and sporadic shooting or, rather, heavy shooting. There was shooting of greater intensity, and that went on until the end of the operation. All this was observed by the verifiers from their positions, the ones that I indicated earlier on, and these are the positions. On the map, I think this would be one position, and another one would be over here, near this Kostanje military police position. I don't know if I've made myself clear enough.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sufficiently clear. I think we can move on to the third map now, which shows us the situation up until 1530 hours.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The legend is the same as the one that applied on the previous map. On this map here we see the situation between 10.15 and 10.30 hours. During that period of time, the police took control of almost the entire village of Racak. Between 10.30 and 1200 hours, two more terrorists were killed in the middle of the village, in a bunker that we didn't know about, didn't know existed, or we can -- it wasn't actually a bunker. It was a shelter of some sort. At 10.30, or, rather, between 10.30 and 12.30, two more lost their lives around their staff headquarters, and with that, the operation was completed. From 1100 hours until 1530 hours, the police that were moving forward in the village had heavy attacks from the Hadzovici and Luzak villages. And Luzak. That is to say the terrorists launched an all-out attack with all the weapons they had at their disposal, and they shelled the oncoming police with 60-millimetres mortars and hand-held rocket launchers of 500 millimetres. Several vehicles were damaged, and one policeman was killed -- was wounded in the clash. At 1530 hours, a team -- or, rather, a little before 1530, an on-site investigation team led by Danica Marinkovic went on site, together with the Urosevac SUP team as well as the deputy public prosecutor -- As soon as this started from all sides --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, you didn't enunciate the name of the deputy public prosecutor so we see an empty space in the transcript, and I must --

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ismet Sufta.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Could you be clearer when pronouncing the names, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the deputy public prosecutor, district public prosecutor. As soon as the investigation started, it had to be interrupted for security and safety reasons. At a meeting before the operation was launched, it was agreed and it was provided that a group should stay at the positions reached until a Special Police Unit platoon arrived, which would take up its positions until the investigation was completed. However, at around 1530 hours, the leader of the operation, Goran Radosavljevic, appeared and ordered the Operative Pursuit Group to leave the trench and the positions adopted to go to the village, although the policemen who were in charge of taking over those positions had not yet arrived at the trenches to take up their positions there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, explain this to me. He appeared. Where was -- where had he been up until then? How did he appear?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he was before that. I didn't have any radio communication with him nor did I see him, but according to information I gathered later on, information coming to me from my associates and the late Miro Mekic, for example, the company commander, he appeared at the point in time when the operation had been completed, to all intents and purposes, and issued orders that the pursuit group withdraw without the previous arrival of the police group that wants to take their place. At the same time, the terrorists who were nearby, near these positions, stormed the trenches and all hell broke loose. There was shooting from all available weaponry, and in five minutes' time the entire team had to pull out the investigation team confronted with this onslaught. So there was an error made in the commands issued. Otherwise, the investigation would have been completed, and there would have been no space for any kind of manipulation. And I stand -- state with full responsibility that the verifiers observed the entire course of this operation, of all these events. There was not a single point in Racak that they could not see from their one position or their second position or their third position. And the television crews that were on the spot filmed the entire course of the operation. I think there were two television crews, in actual fact. A moment ago you said there was the Reuters crew. I didn't know about Reuters, but I did know about Associated Press, that they were there on the spot. Associated Press filmed the entire course of the operation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see any of them personally, contact them in any way?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the representative of the Associated Press when we were getting the investigation team out of the village of Racak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Unfortunately, we don't have their film.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the Court can obtain their film too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janicevic. Just now you described the chronology on these maps. As for this chronology, did you compile some kind of official document about it; and, if so, when? I'm talking about the chronology.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An official document about the anti-terrorist action in Racak and everything that happened after that was what I compiled, I think on the 19th of January, and the development of the chronology of events in Racak, and that was sent to the district public prosecutor's office, describing or, rather, in line with their request. I also submitted it to the MUP staff. One copy stayed in my office. At the request of the working group of the Ministry, I had to hand over that copy of the report to them, and unfortunately, I don't know what happened to it. But what remained in the file is just a part or, rather -- no. The entire chronology is there except for this one page, the last page that is missing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Let me just have a look at something.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Can I ask, Mr. Nice, is it news to you that there is film in the hands of two news agencies of the actual events in Racak?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Nice, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there anything you can do to ascertain whether there's any more material available?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My machinery is intermittent. You can be quite confident that I will do everything that I possibly can, and the -- no. You can be quite sure I will do -- but these things take some time, especially as we're now on a Friday. Incidentally, while I'm on my feet, I did raise with the legal officer at the beginning of the week whether the collection of Racak materials that we put together for earlier witnesses had been retained by the Court. I don't know whether it has. I would be helped by knowing that because presentation of such material as I may use for asking questions might depend on whether I know there's an existing file that I could add pages to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We'll have that checked out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, this chronology that you're talking about just now, is that contained in tab 71?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the chronology compiled on the 19th of January.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, that was already exhibited as D299, tab 397. It was already admitted into evidence. But I just wish to clarify a few things. I want to have them clarified by Mr. Janicevic because he explained a moment ago that he wrote that chronology.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So could you please first explain to me this missing page. You mentioned a while ago that the last page is missing. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, just one page is missing, the last one, at that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Are you sure that it's your document?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm absolutely sure that it's my document, a document I compiled and sent on to the institutions in charge and to my superior officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So on that last page we could otherwise see the date, your signature, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you compile this?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 19th of January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me just have a look. I think it's on page 5 of this chronology of yours, somewhere around the middle of the page. You say that this analysis pertains to the period from the 15th until the 19th. So this chronology covers the period from the 15th to the 19th.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 19th is the last day when there was fierce fighting in the area.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. All right. Since you compiled this chronology, do you think that there is something of particular significance that should be indicated, something that has not been mentioned so far in your evidence concerning Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that I've spoken about everything very exhaustively until now, everything that has to do with these events.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, my request is that these tabs that we looked at just now be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You referred to tab 70.1, 2, and 3.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Since 71 has already been exhibited. And I've mentioned the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, they're admitted, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, tell us, as you were establishing all the facts, especially in view of what the district public prosecutor requested from Pristina, did you take some steps; and, if so, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Even without the request of the district public prosecutor, as a rule, after every anti-terrorist action or any action, for that matter, an assessment had to be made and possible evidence had to be gathered about possible accidental omissions or intentional omissions in the work of the police. When I received the request of the district public prosecutor about collecting preliminary information, I asked the company commander and the commanders of the platoons to submit their reports. I myself spoke to several policemen and squad leaders as to whether excessive authority was used or whether there was any abuse of authority during the anti-terrorist action in Racak. According to what I learned, I could not come to the conclusion that there were any omissions or that there was any unlawful action or that there was anything done that was not in line with the code of conduct of the police at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you've just mentioned the reports of the commander of the 6th Company of the Special Police Unit and of the platoon leaders, were these reports done in writing?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the reports were done in writing. If you remember, a moment ago I said, when you asked me about the plan and about measures taken against members of the police, I said that a working group had been established in order to determine the responsibility of members of the police in all anti-terrorist actions, not only in relation to Racak. These reports that I collected from members of the police and from their superior officers were submitted to the MUP staff or, rather, this working group that operated within the staff in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. And in addition to your report which, as you've explained just now, was based on the reports of the company commander, the platoon leaders, the representatives of the Operative Pursuit Group, did the MUP staff respond to the request to collect information, the one submitted by the district public prosecutor in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure that that was done.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the MUP staff also responded to this request from the district prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Let me just have a look at something. What about tab 72 that you have in front of you? Does it contain a document that is related to what you've been telling us just now?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Tab 72 is explanation of the circumstances under which the crime of terrorism, stipulated in Article 125 of the Criminal Code of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, was committed on the 10th of January, 1999, in the village of Slivovo and the 15th of January, 1999, in the village of Racak, municipality of Stimlje.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, this was already admitted as D299, tab 396.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what is contained in this document of the Ministry of the Interior, its headquarters in Pristina, everything that is mentioned here, does it fully correspond to what you know about these events?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it fully corresponds to what I know. Let me just say that the ambush that was organised on the 10th of January to kill a policeman was the last one in a series of terrorist actions that were carried out by terrorists in the municipality of Stimlje and Urosevac over a period of six months prior to these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, do you know who wrote this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document of the working group of the Ministry of the Interior that worked in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I proceed, Mr. Kwon?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In this document, the village of Slivovo is mentioned. What happened in Slivovo on that 10th of January?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 10th of January, in Slivovo, in the early morning hours the terrorists ambushed a police patrol from Stimlje and fired at a vehicle that was moving. On that occasion, Svetislav Przic, a policeman from the Stimlje police station, was seriously wounded, and two days later he died at the hospital in Pristina due to the injuries sustained then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. What is contained in this document under tab 73?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, this was admitted as D299, tab 395.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a plan of the realisation of operative tactical measures and investigations. Number 1 is identification of the terrorist group, its members and activities in the territory of the village of Racak. This plan was compiled by the working group of the Ministry of the Interior headed by Major General Dragan Ilic, from Belgrade, who at the time was in Pristina, in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. And members of the group were Miroljub Nikolic and Vladimir Aleksic. That's from the centre at the ministry. On the basis of this plan, this report was compiled, clarifying the circumstances under which the crime of terrorism was committed. That is one of these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it's time for the break. I take it, Mr. Milosevic, that you'll be concluded -- concluding your examination-in-chief sometime during the next session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'll try to go through the remaining questions as fast as possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We are adjourned for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: --- Upon resuming at 12:43 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: There is a matter of some importance, nothing to do with this witness's evidence, that I would desire to raise today. I think it will probably take about five minutes but no more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: At the end of the day's proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: As Your Honour pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Nice, you asked us about Racak material. Were you referring to the compilation -- the compilation you gave us in connection with Jasovic's evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I have that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I also corrected myself on one point. We were indeed aware, of course, of Reuters being the potential providers of one film from the moment that that exhibit had been indexed on that basis, and indeed a request for further assistance from Reuters has already been sent on behalf of the Office of the Prosecution, so far with no results but matters will be pursued. I think Reuters may be particularly problematic. I'm sure what their present status is. We'll pursue Associated Press today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we're working towards your concluding sometime in the middle of this session.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That will not be possible, unfortunately, Mr. Robinson. I've just looked through my notes, and I have a number of questions that I cannot complete in that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, when I was asking you about the army, you explained that you only notified the army to avoid friendly fire, to avoid fire of the army on police forces. Now, tell me, since certain witnesses called by Mr. Nice, primarily John Crosland, whose transcript is in tab 74 - the transcript of his testimony, I mean - he claims, along with a number of other witnesses, that the army of Yugoslavia provided artillery support to the shelling of Racak village that went on all day. Can you comment on this claim since you were about a kilometre away from Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can say this is completely untrue. What kind of fool would shell a village where the police were engaged, if you think logically. Would the army fire on the police? It's absolutely untrue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. The police was there from early in the morning?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From 6.30 a.m.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. In paragraph 66 of the indictment, we read, inter alia, that the forces of the FRY and Serbia kept firing on the fleeing villagers.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That also is untrue. There were no more than a hundred people in the village, including the terrorists. Second, the police had no reason to fire on the locals. They were in their houses. They were left alone there. The police was instead responding to the fire of the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were any civilians killed by accident in this exchange of fire?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. According to our information, all those who were killed were members of the terrorist organisation in Racak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, tell me, since you have viewed the photographs of Mr. Nice and you explained the location of the verifiers, from your knowledge of the terrain, was it possible for the verifiers to fail to notice some alleged massacre in the gully?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I have shown from the two locations of the verifiers, they had to see everything that was happening, not only Racak but a circle of 500 to 1.000 metres around Racak, because it is not a wooded area. They had to know that fire had been opened on the police, and it took a lot of shooting for that number of people to be killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did the vantage points of the verifiers offer a good view of the gully and all the other locations where fire was opened?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be seen clearly even with the naked eye.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, at the time of this operation did you have contact with your operational locations, and did you get any additional information either before or after the operation concerning activities in that area?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had regular contacts on a daily basis with all operatives on the terrain, but on the 16th of January specifically I had contacts with the operatives in Racak who were later killed by the terrorists, and they informed me that on the night of the 15th the terrorist group that had arrived from Petrovo village and Luzak village set aside a certain number of the bodies of the terrorists who had been killed and buried them in the Muslim cemetery during the night, the cemetery in Malopoljce. The bodies left unburied were those that belonged to the inhabitants of Racak, the terrorists who were natives of Racak.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of your involvement in this anti-terrorist operation, do you know anything about the presence of verifiers on the surrounding hills and whether some of the verifiers had been in this area at the critical time?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of January I received a written report from the police patrol that manned the checkpoint outside the entrance to Racak, if you go from Stimlje towards Racak, and the report said briefly that around 2100 hours a white jeep holding Ambassador Walker passed through the checkpoint, and there were another two persons and a driver inside the vehicle. Half an hour later, the vehicle came back the same way with only the driver and Ambassador Walker inside, whereas the other two persons remained either in Racak or in that area. And the staff of that Nerodimlje terrorist group was also on the same axis.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What date does this refer to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the evening of the 14th January, around 2100 hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's on the eve of the anti-terrorist action.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have this written report?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regrettably, I don't have either that report or many other documents that would have been useful for this trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The witness of the other side that I mentioned already, John Crosland, claimed that he had seen William Walker in Racak on the 15th of January, on the day of the anti-terrorist operation. Let me just find -- we have it in the transcript, tab 74. It's part of the testimony of John Crosland. He says that he had seen, that's on page 8003, I asked him: "[In English] A moment ago, you said you saw members of the Verification Mission, and you said that during your examination-in-chief as well. So in Racak on 15th of January. And your answer was that you had seen them and that you believe you saw Ambassador Walker as well; is that right? "Answer: That is correct, Mr. Milosevic, yes."

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no reason not to believe Colonel Crosland, because he is a member of the British army. But I claim, I assert that prior to 6.30 on the 15th of January William Walker could not have been in Racak because there were combat activities going on. There was a clash with terrorists. Maybe Mr. Crosland confused it with a period after the completion of the operation. It's possible that he had seen Mr. Walker on the evening of the 15th, where they met, because Crosland was on his way down to Racak at that time. Maybe he also confused it with the 14th of January, in the evening, when he had visited Racak. At least, that would coincide with the information that I have.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this transcript of the testimony of John Crosland from pages -- from page 7945 to 8006.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: It's part of the transcript, so you don't need to tender it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, then. So it has the same value then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Of course. Well, it's there. It's there for us to make of it what we will.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I suppose you will judge it as it is standing on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, please look at tab 75, and I will read -- I will ask you only a few questions. I have only the Serbian translation here, but this is a document produced by Mr. Nice, because I see it bears an ERN number, U0003313, under tab 75. That is the translation of a KLA document of the 121st Brigade Kuma, dated the 30th of January, 1999. Novo Selo. What does this refer to? It deals with a number of issues, but could you please just read the beginning.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Report of the Chief of Staff of the 121st Brigade, dedicated to the Chief of Staff of the KLA. Pursuant to the oral order of the chief of the operative staff of the KLA of the 14th of January, 1999, at 2330 hours, concerning combat readiness --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "-- concerning combat readiness --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Could you please slow down, the interpreters are asking.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "... concerning combat readiness and preparations for attack of the 2nd Company of the 121st Battalion, the following work report was compiled: "On the above-mentioned day, the chief of the operative staff of the KLA ordered that personnel be prepared to move in the direction of the Crnoljevo gorge and Stimlje fir trees for attack on enemy forces on the 15th of January, 1999, with the objective of assisting our forces attacked by the enemy in Racak, Petrovo, and Belince." Should I continue? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Let us deal with these dates. They are important. Do you know who this Dragan Shaban is?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is a member of a terrorist group that was active in the area of Lipjan. He had committed a lot of crimes that cost a lot of lives. It says in the penultimate line before the signature, "Death to the enemy, freedom to the people." It's the same as back in those times, from the previous war, "Death to fascism, freedom to the people."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you understand from these lines that you just read?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It follows from this passage that the terrorists knew about the impending anti-terrorist operation in Racak or the surrounding area. They didn't know exactly where it would happen, in Racak or Petrovo or Belince, but they eventually found out from some source. I don't know which source. According to what is written here, they intended to mount an attack on the members of the army of Yugoslavia who were stationed at Canovica hill, because they probably thought that the army would take part in the anti-terrorist operations and they wanted to help out their own forces located in Racak, Petrovo, and Belince.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This passage that you quoted here says: "For attack against enemy forces on the 15th of January, with the objective of assisting our forces attacked by the enemy in Racak, Petrovo, and Belince."

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, Mr. Robinson, I don't have an English translation, but I suppose that since I got this document from the opposite side and it bears an ERN number, I suppose, and I hope, they have an English translation, and I don't think it is necessary to quote any more from this document. I would just like to tender it, tab 75.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, marked for identification pending translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, how many terrorists do you say were in Racak?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to our intelligence gathered through operative sources, there were around 80.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, on the 15th of January. No, I mean in general, around 80 terrorists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: On the 15th.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Around 80 on the 15th of January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that a realistic complement of men to take on not only the police but the army who are going to engage in an anti-terrorist operation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I never said that it was a joint operation. The anti-terrorist operation was conducted by the police alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that, but you said that this document we've been referring to indicated that they expected the police and the army to be involved.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But this document of the 121st Brigade Kuma was not linked to that staff, to that operations zone, Nerodimlje. This particular unit was linked to the Pastrik operation zone, which is part of the Lipjan municipality. It's a brigade from an entirely different area, different zone. 121st Brigade Kuma. Whereas here we're dealing with the 161st Brigade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought you read that on the 14th of January "the chief of the operative staff of the KLA ordered the personnel be prepared to move in the direction of the Crnoljevo gorge and Stimlje for attack on enemy forces on the 15th of January with the objective of assisting our forces attacked by the enemy in Racak, Petrovo." Is that not what you read to us?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And are you not saying that's an indication that the KLA were coming to -- to Racak in anticipation of an attack by both the police -- an anti-terrorist operation by the police and the army? In their minds by the police and the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an instruction by the operative staff to a completely different brigade. In Racak, part of the 161st Brigade was stationed, whereas this brigade was a brigade working in another area altogether.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I understand that, but the point you seem to be making was that the KLA knew that something was going to happen, and they eventually worked out, according to your evidence, that it was going to be in Racak. Now, if that's the position, what I'm asking you is is it realistic of them to send 80 people to deal with an anticipated anti-terrorist operation by both the police and the army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, had the operation not been performed the way it had been, not 100 but 500 policemen and soldiers wouldn't have been able to take control of those positions. First of all, because the trenches in which the terrorists were located on two levels, there was shooting coming from the trenches, and the police that were to take control of that most probably would have all been killed or 50 per cent would have been killed had they taken part in that kind of operation. That's the first point. Secondly, this is not my piece of information, my report. I see this for the first time. This is quite a different brigade here, different operative zone. They had their own system of reporting and information amongst themselves, and this particular brigade, the 161st Brigade, was operative on the right-hand side of Crnoljevska gorge or the Suva Reka-Stimlje road in the direction of Petrastica, Caracica [phoen], Duga, and so on, Lipovacka, Suma, that axis. So their area of operation was over there, and in their area of operation was part of the operative combat group of the army of Yugoslavia, the 333rd Motorised Brigade -- 243rd Motorised Brigade. So according to what it says here, they had planned to attack the army. They were planning to attack the army at Canovica hill, which was in Borovina or Jele [phoen], Jelovina [phoen]. Have I made myself clear? I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, according to this document, did they know that there would be an attack or an anti-terrorist operation would take place on 15th of January on the part of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Kwon, according to what it says here, I think that in a way they did acquire that knowledge. Now, how they came by that knowledge, I don't know. As we had people amongst them, I assume they had people amongst us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. What I heard from you is that they might have known that there would be an attack sometime. My question is: Did they know there would be an attack on 15th, so that's why they're preparing a counter-attack in advance?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know that. I don't know whether they knew or not. But according to what it says here in this report, most probably they did know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, may I just draw your attention to one point, a detail, if I can call it that. The witness said that in Racak there were about 80 members of the KLA, and from this document of this brigade we can see that from that brigade the group of 80 in Racak were to be reinforced by another group of men. Reinforcements were to be sent to them. And what he read out here in this document, it says an attack against enemy forces on the 15th of January. So they planned the attack.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Milosevic. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honours, before we move on, the fact that a document was provided by our side sometimes says nothing about its provenance or necessarily its integrity. All I can tell you about this document is that it was provided under Rule 68, having been obtained from a deputy head of state security in Serbia. So it's a document that originated in the state security services of Serbia. It was provided to this office and then was provided under Rule 68. That's all we know about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What happened on the 16th of January? You explained to us that on the 15th of January, in the afternoon, there was an attempt to carry out an on-site investigation, if I followed you correctly. Now tell us what happened on the 16th of January, when the investigating judge appeared again to conduct the investigation.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th of January, the same team plus the investigating judge came to the location, but at the access to the village they were fired upon by the terrorists and they weren't even able to approach the village, get close to the village at all. So they went back, and the investigation was not carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we have been through what happened on the 16th of January. Unless this witness has something new, something fresh, we don't wish to hear it. You should move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us just clarify one point. Mention was made here of a discussion where this witness was mentioned, a discussion between Judge Danica Marinkovic and General Drewienkiewicz, and I wish the witness to clarify the matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I will allow you to ask that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the investigation conducted on the 17th of January; and if not, why could it not have been conducted?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The investigation was not conducted on the 17th either because the team could not reach the location because of terrorist attacks, or the terrorist attack.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when did Drewienkiewicz, the deputy head of the Verification Mission, arrive at the Stimlje police station?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drewienkiewicz arrived, I think at around 10.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the date?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 17th of January, at about 10.00.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you present at the time?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you attend the talk between Judge Marinkovic and Mr. Drewienkiewicz?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did Mr. Drewienkiewicz ask Judge Marinkovic to do?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said that in Racak there were no terrorists, there were no armed persons, and that Danica Marinkovic could freely enter Racak with him and conduct the on-site investigation and the Verification Mission would serve as protection. Danica refused to do that, and she asked that the law be abided by, which demanded that she as the investigating judge be there, the deputy public prosecutor, the investigation team, and the police to provide security and the unhampered work of the team. He refused to discuss the matter further and insisted that she go with him, that she accompany him. Danica refused and said that she would go if the police went with her, with an escort, a police escort. Mr. Drewienkiewicz at one point said that if you go to carry out the investigation with the police, you will cause bloodshed, and you will be responsible for having done that. She asked, "Well, what shall we do now? What bloodshed are you talking about? A moment ago you said that there were no armed persons, no armed civilians or terrorists there, that the village was practically empty, and now you're mentioning bloodshed." And he said, "Yes, but there are armed civilians over there." And I joined in and asked -- I said General, I asked, "General, a moment ago you said there was nobody there, and now you claim there are armed civilians there. How is it in your country, in England? Don't you call armed civilians terrorists?" And his answer to me was, "Don't compare my country and what happens over there with what is happening here." And I asked him, "Aren't terrorists the same the world over?" And he kept silent. He didn't wish to answer. And after that, Danica ordered that the team go out to conduct the investigation. They left the office, and they went on location, and they returned just a half an hour later with a damaged vehicle and their job not finished.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Then I'll skip the questions related to the on-site investigation. We heard testimony from Judge Marinkovic and the investigation took place on the 18th of January. I'm sure you'll remember that.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What about the members of the investigation team? Were any of them wounded, injured, killed perhaps?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Miro Mekic was killed, the assistant commander of the Urosevac police station, on the 19th, after the on-site investigation, on the 19th of January, in holding the positions for further investigation and looking into traces of crimes. That was the position that was taken. And two policemen were also seriously wounded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So one was killed -- one person was killed, two persons seriously wounded. All right. Now, what did the Albanian officials say about the terrorists in Racak? Can we see a short piece of footage where the Racak commemoration took place, tab 76?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: No translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is no translation, no transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Will you stop, stop the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The soundtrack is in Albanian, note the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Are we able to get any translation from the interpreters?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We have no transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can the Albanian booth help?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Yes, we will try to provide some interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Let it be played from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] For five days on end it is shown that this might have an influence in the international conference on Kosovo, and after several days, painful days of talks, finally we managed to have a special funeral for those people in that part of the village, to have the free funeral, a dignified funeral attended by all those who'd like to attend the funeral, including those mass media and the international representatives present in Kosovo. We managed that this event also had its own echo in the final fate of the people of Kosovo. Of course, our final demand was that the group we contacted and the OSCE representatives, so that we wanted the William Walker, Ambassador William Walker to take part in that funeral and that was about 24 hours. At that time we received confirmation that William Walker had postponed a very important visit."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What's the question arising?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "[Voiceover] William Walker, who never made a career on behalf of Albanians, in February 1999 before the participants of the funeral in Racak, he said: 'This crime -- this crime against humanity. The deaths in Racak demand justice and justice must be seen to be done. The graves before me tragically represent, to me at least, the madness, the appalling waste, and the futility of unrestrained violence.' "In November 1999 he visited against Kosovo and found himself amongst the citizens of Racak but now under new circumstances, in freedom. On this occasion, he paid homage to and placed wreaths of flowers."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On this video, we were to hear the statements of Albanian officials with respect to the events in Racak, but there was probably some confusion because this excerpt was not the important one that I wanted to have you see with respect to the questions I wished to ask. I think there was some mix-up there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have wasted some time, Mr. Milosevic. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That would -- is how it seems to be to me too.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Might I be allowed to say something, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Who is that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With respect to this video, may I be allowed to say something?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No. It's not what Mr. Milosevic had in mind. Let Mr. Milosevic put his next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have any knowledge about what the Albanian officials said about the terrorists killed in Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know is that all the terrorists that -- who were killed were buried in one place, and from this footage we can see that it was in the -- in the mosque, every casket was covered with an Albanian flag. When civilians are killed, the flag is not used. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. The doctor who allegedly carried out the autopsies of the bodies that were found on the spot speaks about some kind of post-mortem which he conducted and establishing the cause of death, extracting organs of the individual casualties, and so on. I can't remember just now what it was he said, but what I have just seen -- well, I lived there for many years, 50 years, in fact, and I never saw a civilian who had died or been killed being -- that their coffin is covered with an Albanian flag, whereas here in the mosque we see that all the bodies have been covered with the Albanian flag.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. I think we can move on. Take a look at what we have in tab 77 now, please. It is a handwritten daily report, and we have here a translation into Serbian. It's very short. What does it say here in this daily report of the 161st Brigade, Ahmet Kaciku?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This brigade was named after the commander of the 163rd Brigade who was killed in Racak on the day when Miro Mekic, assistant commander, was killed. The report is dated -- or, rather, this is the report of some commander of theirs, Daja and Dula, who were referring to Bagdasit. And they --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, it doesn't say anything about the origin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, please elicit evidence about the provenance of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, do you know anything about this document and its origin?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had it in my hands in 1999, in the month of April. It was seized during an anti-terrorist action in the village of Jezerce. In addition to this document, there is a series of other documents that were seized there, and they were all handed over to the state security department in Urosevac at the time and were forwarded to the headquarters of the DB in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. This unit, I mean you say that their material was seized later. And as we can see, this unit has mortars and what is mentioned is the geographic area that we talked about in Racak. This unit and this equipment, does that have anything to do with the shelling of Racak as the anti-terrorist attacks evolved in Racak?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, of course.

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 15th of January when the anti-terrorist action in Racak was taking place, the only parties doing any kind of shelling were the terrorists. 60-millimetre mortars. At that time, those are the only ones they had. And they also had hand-held rocket launchers of 500 millimetres. And of course an anti-aircraft gun, 12.7 millimetres, in two positions; above Racak on the hill of Krcine, and on Crveni Put towards Petrovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are you reading from this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No. I'm speaking from memory. This is a document that is from a later period, that is to say it is dated the 28th of April. If necessary, I will read it out. May I read the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I don't want it read out. If Mr. Milosevic wants evidence from it, he can ask you to summarise it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: As for this document, how do you know this is a seized document, one of those?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because that was the only time that vast documentation was seized in that operative zone, in Jezerce. This is the operative zone of Nerodimlje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you bring this document with you when you came to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was provided from the headquarters of the state security service, that is to say from the BIA, in June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Provided to whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what the advisors told me in Belgrade, the Defence advisors that is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The associates, legal associates of the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Momo Raicevic personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Janicevic, in this document number 78, do we see some kind of diary written, handwritten in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: BOGOLJUB JANICEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From the first notebook we have just a few translations that have to do with the conflict in Racak. Could you please read that out. As for the entire diary, only these few excerpts have been taken.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, elicit evidence about this diary. Where does it come from, who made it, and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the diary of Baskim Ndrecaj. The first notebook, special unit Baskim Ndrecaj participation in action and conflicts. This diary, as you can see on the photocopies, is handwritten in the Albanian language. A few quotations have been extracted here, and my associates received this from our security organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It could have come or been manufactured anywhere. Its reliability is nil. It has no indicia of reliability. It shouldn't be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MS. HIGGINS
utterances.text: Your Honour, perhaps the witness could be asked if he knows anything about the document, just to confirm.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Do you know anything about the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document was also seized at the headquarters of the 161st Brigade of the operations zone of Nerodimlje in Jezerce. Along with all other documents, it was handed over to the state security sector. And then Momo Raicevic, legal advisor, received it from there, of course with a certificate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Had you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had seen it earlier on, and it was at my initiative that this request was filed with the BIA, so that this documentation could be presented in this Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What do you mean by "earlier on"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Earlier on. I saw it earlier on. In 1999, I think. Along with all the other seized documents that the policemen brought to me, I handed it over to the state security department then and then they forwarded it further on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
